Title: Factors influencing neurotrophic effects of electrical stimulation in the deafened developing auditory system.
Stimulus_Type: electrical stimulation from a cochlear implant
Outcome: spiral ganglion neuron density; cochlear nucleus volume; spherical cell size
Evidence_Quote: In cats deafened early in life, effective stimulation of the auditory nerve with complex signals for several months preserves a greater density of SG neurons in the stimulated cochleae as compared to the contralateral deafened ear.

Title: Neonatal nicotine exposure impairs development of auditory temporal processing.
Outcome: gap detection; auditory temporal processing; gap-PPI
Evidence_Quote: Neonatal rats were injected twice per day with saline (control), 1mg/kg nicotine (N-1 mg) or 5 mg/kg nicotine (N-5 mg) from postnatal day 8-12 (P8-P12).

Title: The influence of a sensitive period on central auditory development in children with unilateral and bilateral cochlear implants.
Target_Age: either before age 3.5 years or after age 7 years
Outcome: cortical auditory evoked potential (CAEP) morphology; P1 cortical response latency
Evidence_Quote: We examined the longitudinal development of the cortical auditory evoked potential (CAEP) in 21 children who were fitted with unilateral cochlear implants and in two children who were fitted with bilateral cochlear implants either before age 3.5 years or after age 7 years.

Title: Sustained cadherin 23 expression in young and adult cochlea of normal and hearing-impaired mice.
Outcome: cadherin 23 expression; cadherin 23 localization to stereocilia
Evidence_Quote: Furthermore, CDH23Delta68 expression levels in young and adult cochlea are similar among normal and hearing deficient strains (C3HeB/FeJ, C57BL/6J and BUB/BnJ).

Title: A model for estimating ultrasound attenuation along the propagation path to the fetus from backscattered waveforms.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: ultrasound attenuation; total attenuation estimation
Evidence_Quote: Herein, a method for determining the total attenuation from the backscattered power spectrum from the developing fetus is proposed.

Title: Middle ear and cochlear disorders result in different DPOAE growth behaviour: implications for the differentiation of sound conductive and cochlear hearing loss.
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones (f2 2.0-8.0 kHz; L2 15-60 dB SPL; f2/f1=1.2)
Outcome: DPOAE growth behaviour differentiates middle-ear from cochlear dysfunction
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE I/O-functions were recorded in a wide primary tone level range at up to 8 f2 frequencies between 2.0 and 8.0 kHz (15 dB SPL < L2< 60 dB SPL; L1=0.46 L2 + 41 dB SPL; f2/f1=1.2) in guinea pigs

Title: Trophic effects of insulin-like growth factor-I (IGF-I) in the inner ear.
Outcome: auditory thresholds; auditory neuron loss; hearing loss
Evidence_Quote: Mice lacking IGF-I lose many auditory neurons and present increased auditory thresholds at early postnatal ages.

Title: Auditory function associated with Col11a1 haploinsufficiency in chondrodysplasia (cho) mice.
Outcome: auditory brainstem response (ABR) thresholds
Evidence_Quote: There was no difference in ABR thresholds for click and tone burst stimuli between cho/+ and +/+ mice at all ages.

Title: Mice lacking the B1 subunit of H+ -ATPase have normal hearing.
Outcome: hearing; auditory brainstem response
Evidence_Quote: Auditory brainstem response tests revealed normal hearing in mice lacking Atp6b1.

Title: Chronic placental insufficiency has long-term effects on auditory function in the guinea pig.
Target_Age: guinea pigs (tested at 8 weeks of age)
Stimulus_Type: clicks (33 pps) and tone pips for ABR
Outcome: long-term ABR effects of chronic placental insufficiency
Evidence_Quote: Stimuli consisted of 100 micros clicks, presented at 33 pulses per second (pps) and tone pip stimuli at frequencies of 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 kHz.

Title: Developmental changes in physiological properties in the rat's dorsal nucleus of the lateral lemniscus.
Target_Age: rat pups at postnatal days 4-8; postnatal days 10-12; postnatal days 16-18
Stimulus_Type: electrical stimulation of the lateral lemniscus and commissure of Probst
Outcome: postsynaptic potentials (PSPs); intrinsic membrane properties; synaptic responses
Evidence_Quote: Postsynaptic potentials (PSPs), with excitatory predominance, were elicited by electrical stimulation of the lateral lemniscus and commissure of Probst throughout the three age groups.

Title: Cisplatin ototoxicity in developing gerbils.
Target_Age: young gerbils (first exposed at 2 weeks of age; measured at 6 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: cisplatin dosing (1-3 doses) with DPOAE/ABR monitoring
Outcome: dose-related cisplatin ototoxicity (DPOAE/ABR threshold elevation)
Evidence_Quote: A tendency for a bimodal distribution of DPOAE and ABR responses was also observed in the D1 group, at frequencies below 8 kHz.

Title: Postnatal expression of the alpha-thyroid hormone receptor in the rat cochlea.
Target_Age: rat from the first postnatal day up to day 30
Outcome: alpha-thyroid hormone receptor expression in cochlea
Evidence_Quote: Staining could be detected during all stages investigated from the first postnatal day up to day 30

Title: Temporary threshold shifts induced by low-pass and high-pass filtered noises in fetal sheep in utero.
Stimulus_Type: low-pass and high-pass filtered noise (cut-off frequency 1.0 kHz), approx. 120 dB SPL, 16 h
Outcome: temporary ABR threshold shifts after filtered-noise exposure
Evidence_Quote: Auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) were obtained from nine late gestational age fetal sheep in utero before and after a 16-h exposure to low-pass (cut-off frequency 1.0 kHz) and high-pass (cut-off frequency 1.0 kHz) noises (approximately 120 dB sound pressure level, recorded in air). Bone-conduction ABRs were elicited by broadband clicks and 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 kHz tone bursts.

Title: Thyroxine affects physiological and morphological development of the ear.
Stimulus_Type: distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPE) and ABR clicks; stimulus intensities 50 and 70 dB SPL
Outcome: effect of thyroxine on onset/development of DPE, ABR and ear morphology
Evidence_Quote: DPEs were recorded at an earlier postnatal age to high (8 kHz) frequencies and progressed to lower (3 kHz) frequencies with age. ABRs to high-intensity clicks were recorded at least 2 days before DPEs, although DPE onset at 8 kHz preceded adult-like ABR thresholds. Both ABR and DPEs appeared earlier in the hyperthyroid rats. Histological evidence showed earlier morphological development of the ear in these animals. ABR thresholds and DPE amplitudes matured at a slower rate in the experimental group despite their earlier onset. There was no difference in ABR and DPE thresholds between adult hyperthyroid and control rats. However, in the experimental group, DPEs had smaller amplitudes to high (70 dB SPL) and to low (50 dB SPL) stimulus intensities at low frequencies.

Title: Pharmacokinetics of kanamycin in the developing rat.
Outcome: kanamycin pharmacokinetics; elimination half-life
Evidence_Quote: We characterized the pharmacokinetics of kanamycin in the serum of 12- and 25-day-old rats

Title: The perception of speech sounds recorded within the uterus of a pregnant sheep.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: speech intelligibility; phoneme intelligibility
Evidence_Quote: The intelligibility of speech stimuli recorded within the uterus of a pregnant sheep was determined perceptually using a group of untrained judges.

Title: Noise induced hearing loss in fetal sheep.
Stimulus_Type: broadband noise, 120 dB SPL for 16 h (exposure of pregnant ewes); ABR clicks and tone bursts via bone oscillator
Outcome: noise-induced ABR threshold elevation in fetal sheep
Evidence_Quote: The auditory brainstem response (ABR) was recorded in utero from chronically instrumented fetal sheep prior to and following exposure of pregnant ewes to intense broadband noise (120 dB SPL for 16 h). ABRs were elicited by clicks and tone bursts (0.5, 1, 2, and 4 kHz) delivered through a bone oscillator

Title: The sensitivity to 3,3'-iminodipropionitrile differs for high- and midfrequency hearing loss in the developing rat.
Outcome: auditory thresholds; adult-like IDPN susceptibility reached ~PND 30-32; early exposure caused high-frequency-selective loss
Evidence_Quote: All animals were tested as adults for auditory thresholds to 5- and 40-kHz tones using reflex modification audiometry.

Title: Development of hearing in neonatal rats: air and bone conducted ABR thresholds.
Stimulus_Type: air-conducted (AC) and bone-conducted (BC) ABR stimuli (levels in dB HL)
Outcome: development of air- and bone-conduction ABR thresholds; air-bone gap resolved by PND 15
Evidence_Quote: ABR to maximal intensity BC stimuli (55 dB above adult rat ABR threshold--55 dB HL*) could be recorded from PND 7-8 while AC responses to 80 dB HL* stimuli, only from PND 11.

Title: Activity patterns of primary auditory-nerve fibres in chickens: development of fundamental properties.
Outcome: development of auditory-nerve fiber activity patterns and tuning characteristics
Evidence_Quote: We have examined the activity patterns of single auditory-nerve fibers in the chicken and tested for possible changes during post-hatching development.
